subject: System Design
title: TCP: Reliable Delivery
description: A fast breakdown of TCP: Reliable Delivery for builders.

hook.text: You download a file. One packet gets lost. TCP detects the loss and resends it automatically.

buildup.text: TCP ensures reliable, ordered delivery. It numbers packets and tracks acknowledgments.

discovery.text: The three-way handshake — SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK — establishes a connection before any data flows.

twist.text: TCP's reliability adds latency. Every packet waits for acknowledgment before the next batch is sent.

climax.text: TCP powers the web, email, and file transfers — anything where losing data is unacceptable.

punchline.text: TCP guarantees every byte arrives, in order, or it retries.

quiz.question: What does the TCP three-way handshake do?
options: Establishes a connection before data transfer begins
